blocks.text: “We’ve decided not to vote. At all,” Vatiswa Zoya said two days before voters in South Africa cast their ballots for new municipal government leaders. “What is the point? We will still sleep hungry.” These very same frustrations are what will lead 22-year-old Lindokuhle Mbandazayo to the polls, although she has yet to decide where to place her cross. “When we vote for councilors, we ask them to fix the area,” Mbandazayo told DW. “The electricity goes off regularly here.
